company: 中原地產 Centaline Property Agency Limited
revenue: unknown (private; c.40,000 staff, 2,000+ offices in 39 cities per unsourced Wikipedia)
marketing_evidence: Heavy property-listing and media advertising in Hong Kong; founder also launched am730 newspaper; no major sports sponsorship found
rationale: Centaline is a large private property agency founded in 1978 by Shih Wing-ching, with offices across Hong Kong, Macau and mainland China. Its revenue is not public, and HK/China property brokerage has limited global F1 synergy.

marketing_evidence: Leisure resort marketing; little sponsorship evidence
rationale: Swandor Hotels & Resorts is a private Turkish operator of all-inclusive resort hotels selling mainly to European and Russian holiday markets. It publishes no financials and has limited F1 synergy beyond hospitality.

marketing_evidence: Vape-product marketing (heavily restricted in most F1 markets)
rationale: Geekvape is a Shenzhen-based maker of vaping devices sold worldwide. Revenue is undisclosed, and tobacco and e-cigarette advertising bans in the EU, UK and many GP host markets severely limit any F1 deal despite the BAT/PMI precedent.

marketing_evidence: B2B retail/channel execution provider; little evidence
rationale: Channelplay is an Indian outsourced retail-execution, merchandising and channel-sales services firm with a large field workforce. It has no consumer brand, operates mainly in India and publishes no financials.

profitability: Profitable: operating income USD 132M, net income USD 52M (2024)
marketing_evidence: Historic associations with sports clubs (MKE Ankaragucu, MKE Kirikkalespor)
rationale: MKE is Turkey's state-owned arms and ammunition maker (100% Ministry of National Defence), with USD 1.14B revenue and USD 52M net income in 2024. It qualifies on revenue, but a state arms manufacturer is a poor fit with F1 audiences and brand-safety norms.

revenue: unknown (private; 3,000+ points of sale, 300+ own stores, 10M+ pieces/yr)
marketing_evidence: Retail brand marketing in Brazil; no major sponsorship found
rationale: Grupo HOPE is a Brazilian lingerie and swimwear group (HOPE, HOPE Resort, Bonjour) with 300+ exclusive stores. It is a domestic apparel brand with undisclosed revenue and only partial overlap with F1's audience.

revenue: unknown (private; revenue CAGR 15% per PAI; 450+ sites, 56,000+ pitches)
funding: Significant minority stake sold to ADIA (reported EUR 600M, 2025)
profitability: Earnings more than tripled under PAI (no figures)
marketing_evidence: Consumer holiday brands across Europe; little sponsorship evidence
rationale: European Camping Group runs mobile-home camping holidays across Europe (450+ sites) and is majority-owned by PAI Partners, with ADIA taking a significant minority stake in 2025 (reported EUR 600M). The money is real, but family camping holidays fit F1's premium positioning poorly.

marketing_evidence: Local restaurant, salon and lifestyle brand marketing; little evidence
rationale: Al Ghalia is a Bahrain hospitality and lifestyle group (casual fine dining, Dessange salons, farming, contracting, property). It could act as a Bahrain GP hospitality partner, but it is a local business with undisclosed finances.

valuation: n/a (unlisted; c.55.5% Turkish Armed Forces Foundation)
marketing_evidence: Defence trade-show marketing; no sports sponsorship found
rationale: Roketsan is Turkey's missile and rocket maker, about 55.5% owned by the Turkish Armed Forces Foundation, with USD 1.39B revenue in 2024 (SIPRI) and a preliminary 2025 figure above USD 2B. It qualifies on revenue, but a weapons maker has very weak consumer-sponsorship fit.

marketing_evidence: Tourist-oriented retail brand in Thailand; little sponsorship evidence
rationale: NaRaYa is a Thai maker and retailer of fabric handbags and accessories, sold through its own stores and popular with tourists. It is a modest-price consumer brand with undisclosed revenue and low F1 fit.
